A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
policy transfer is a complex process and that the success of a policy transfer is dependent on a variety of contextual factors.
policy transfer from other countries can be a valuable source of ideas for reform, but the context of the receiving country is important.
the UK Government was not able to learn from its European neighbors, and the policy transfer failed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order for a policy to be successfully transferred, it needs to be tailored to the context in which it is implemented, and the policy transfer process needs to be managed carefully.
policy transfer can work, but only when it is based on a careful assessment of the context of the receiving country and the nature of the policy that is being adopted.

the policy transfer process is not a simple one-way street from a successful policy in one context to a less successful policy in another, and that policy transfer is often not the most appropriate policy instrument to achieve reform.
